cards.title: Introduction to Vue.js Deployment
cards.content:
Deploying a Vue.js application involves building your source code into optimized static assets that can be served by any web server.

Before deployment, you run the production build command:

npm run build

This generates a dist folder containing your minified HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files.

cards.title: Handling SPA Routing
cards.content:
Vue.js applications are typically Single Page Applications (SPAs) using Vue Router in HTML5 History mode.

When deploying to static hosts (like Netlify, Vercel, or GitHub Pages), direct URL navigation or page refreshes can result in 404 Not Found errors.

To fix this, you must configure your server or hosting provider to redirect all unknown paths to your index.html file.

cards.title: Environment Variables in Vue
cards.content:
Vite exposes env variables through import.meta.env.

To prevent accidentally leaking sensitive keys to the client, only variables prefixed with VITE_ are exposed to your Vue code.

# .env.production
VITE_API_URL=https://api.example.com/v1
